extracted.intended_audience: researchers and clinicians who perform journal peer review / prospective peer reviewers
extracted.subtask_description: Practical step-by-step guidance for scientists and clinicians on how to perform high-quality peer review of journal manuscripts, covering invitation decisions, manuscript reading strategy, critique structure, methodological scrutiny, tone, and editor-facing recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timely completion of review
rubrics_metrics.description: The reviewer's timely completion significantly impacts overall efficiency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respond to invitations promptly and meet deadlines; if you cannot, decline rather than not respond. Timeliness is part of the peer review process after editorial screening and assignment to reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Blinding system awareness
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize which blinding system is used: single-blinded, double-blinded, or open review; each carries potential bias risks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Account for how the journal's blinding policy may influence perceived conflicts or bias. Be mindful that knowledge (or anonymity) of author identities can affect evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Motivation and benefits of reviewing
rubrics_metrics.description: Top reasons to serve include participating in the scientific community, reciprocating peer review received, professional expectation, and improving writing skills.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewing offers benefits (e.g., CME credits, career visibility). Use these motivations to guide commitment and quality of effort.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accepting invitations: expertise match
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether the manuscript topics match your expertise before accepting an invitation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you lack sufficient subject-matter expertise, decline so that qualified reviewers can be assigned; identify specific aspects you can or cannot evaluate if accepting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accepting invitations: conflict of interest assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate conflicts of interest prior to accepting: financial, scientific, and personal conflicts may preclude review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclose known conflicts to the editor and decline when conflicts could bias judgment. Examples: direct financial ties, close collaborators, advisor/advisee relationships, or competitive involvement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accepting invitations: deadline feasibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether you can meet the requested deadline before accepting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Declining is better than accepting and failing to deliver; propose realistic alternative timelines only if you can meet them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manuscript reading strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommended approach: read once for overview, take a break, reread for methodology, then reread for writing quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Perform a literature search during preparation to verify novelty and identify related work. Taking staged readings helps separate comprehension, methodological critique, and editorial/writing edits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Literature search to verify novelty
rubrics_metrics.description: Conduct a literature search to verify novelty and identify related work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the search to detect missing citations, prior art, or claims of novelty that are unsupported. Note related studies that should be cited or contrasted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review structure: summary, major, and minor comments
rubrics_metrics.description: Structure recommended: Summary paragraph (3-5 sentences), Major comments (numbered, most important first), Minor comments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Start with a concise summary demonstrating comprehension. Number major comments and place the most important first to help editors and authors prioritize changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Major comment: relevance and journal fit
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess the manuscript's relevance and fit for the journal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advise whether the manuscript advances the journal's scope or audience. If out-of-scope, recommend rejection or transfer per journal norms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Major comment: ethical concerns
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify and raise ethical concerns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Flag ethical issues (e.g., human subjects protections, consent, animal welfare, plagiarism, data fabrication). Recommend editorial actions if serious ethical problems are present.

rubrics_metrics.name: Major comment: Introduction quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate the Introduction for clarity, context, and justification of study aims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check whether the background frames the problem, cites relevant literature, and leads logically to the study objectives or hypotheses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Major comment: Methods quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess Methods for clarity, completeness, and appropriateness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether study design is appropriate, interventions and measurements are described sufficiently for replication, and procedures are transparent. See related methods-specific scrutiny items (study design, data collection clarity, statistical transparency).

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods scrutiny: study design appropriateness
rubrics_metrics.description: Judge whether the chosen study design is appropriate for the research question.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider design strengths/limitations, potential for bias, and alternative designs that might better answer the question.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods scrutiny: data collection clarity ('what, when, how')
rubrics_metrics.description: Require clear reporting of what data were collected, when, and how.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure sample selection, timing, measurements, instruments, and protocols are described so readers can assess validity and reproducibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods scrutiny: statistical analysis transparency
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure statistical methods are reported transparently.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require specification of models/tests used, assumptions checked, handling of missing data, multiple comparisons, effect estimates with confidence intervals, and reproducible code/data when possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods scrutiny: common biases
rubrics_metrics.description: Detect and comment on common biases: design, information, selection, confounding, analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify potential sources of bias, assess whether authors attempted mitigation (e.g., randomization, blinding, adjustment), and recommend additional analyses or clarifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Major comment: Results quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate Results for transparent reporting of group characteristics and comprehensiveness of analyses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check transparent reporting of baseline/group characteristics, appropriate use of tables/figures, clarity of primary vs secondary analyses, and whether analyses match pre-specified plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Results presentation: visual data representation
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether data are well represented visually.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate clarity and appropriateness of figures and tables, use of error bars/uncertainty measures, and whether visuals support textual claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Major comment: Discussion assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess the Discussion for fair, objective interpretation and appropriate context.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check whether authors place findings within existing literature, avoid overstating conclusions, logically derive conclusions from results, and thoroughly discuss limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discussion requirement: limitations discussion
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors should provide a thorough limitations discussion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure limitations are acknowledged, their likely impact on conclusions is described, and no important caveats are omitted or downplayed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internal validity: design appropriateness and bias detection
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate internal validity by assessing whether the design and conduct support causal and unbiased inference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider threats to internal validity (e.g., confounding, measurement error, selection bias) and whether analyses appropriately account for them.

rubrics_metrics.name: External validity: generalizability
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess the generalizability of the findings to other populations or settings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider sample representativeness, setting-specific factors, and whether authors appropriately limit or generalize their claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tone and professionalism
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviews must be collegial and constructive; constructive suggestions should accompany critiques.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid unprofessional comments (the guide notes '12% of reviews contained unprofessional comments'). Justify opinions to prevent appearance of bias and focus on actionable feedback.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editor recommendation categories
rubrics_metrics.description: Common decision options: Accept, Conditional Acceptance, Minor/Major Revision, Reject, or Reject without review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these categories to summarize overall judgment for the editor, aligning major comments with the recommended decision and indicating required changes to reach acceptance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidential editor comments
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide separate confidential comments to the editor explaining decision rationale and raising concerns not suitable for the authors' version.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this space to assess potential impact (advance field, motivate studies, influence clinical care) and to raise concerns unsupported by direct evidence or to suggest editorial actions; avoid repeating author-facing critiques verbatim unless necessary.
